guide.name: Calendly OAuth Setup and Launch Guide
guide.timeNote: Planning estimate, not a measured setup duration. Assumes existing OAuth callback and Calendly account
guide.review: The reviewed registration instructions distinguish Sandbox testing from Production real-user apps. They do not establish a separate provider approval process or turnaround. Confirm external-production requirements with Calendly before promising a launch date.
guide.scopeNote: The reviewed scope catalog requires scheduled_events:read for scheduled-event and invitee reads. Polling does not need webhooks:write. Calling additional endpoints, such as /users/me, needs a separate scope check.
prerequisites: A Calendly account with access to Developer tools.
The integration's callback URL and a list of intended API endpoints.
Secure storage for the creation credentials and a server-side OAuth handler supporting S256 PKCE.

steps.title: Register a Sandbox app with one callback
steps.detail: Create a Sandbox app in Calendly's Developer tools with exactly one callback and at least one scope. Sandbox permits HTTPS or HTTP on localhost; Production requires HTTPS. Use a separate Production app for real customer data.

steps.title: Save the one-time credentials
steps.detail: Before leaving creation, save the client ID, client secret, and webhook signing key securely. The reviewed documentation says none can currently be viewed again in Developer tools.

steps.title: Use S256 PKCE and authenticate the token exchange
steps.detail: Every app requires S256 PKCE. Send the challenge with authorization; retain the verifier for code exchange. POST code, client_id, redirect_uri, grant_type=authorization_code and code_verifier to https://auth.calendly.com/oauth/token. Server apps also use HTTP Basic with client ID and client secret.

steps.title: Confirm external-production requirements
steps.detail: The reviewed registration instructions distinguish Sandbox testing from Production use, but do not establish a separate review process or turnaround. Ask Calendly whether the selected scopes and audience have additional production requirements before promising launch.

blockers.title: Missing Scope Error
blockers.detail: Verify that the scopes requested during installation include all required by the endpoint you are calling. (Source: s5) Confirm that the user granted all requested scopes.
blockers.resolution: Reauthorize the app to request additional scopes.

blockers.title: The callback must fit the selected environment
blockers.detail: Each Calendly app accepts exactly one redirect URI. Sandbox permits HTTPS or HTTP on localhost; Production requires HTTPS.
blockers.resolution: For local HTTP testing, use a Sandbox app and a localhost callback. For real customers, use a separate Production app with an HTTPS callback. Keep the registered redirect URI consistent in the authorization and token requests.

blockers.title: Production eligibility is not established by registration alone
blockers.detail: The fetched registration instructions do not settle additional requirements for the intended external launch.
blockers.resolution: Ask Calendly support about the exact audience, scopes, and Production app configuration. Submit a review only if Calendly confirms one is required.

agentCan: Fetch public documentation and identify relevant registration, scope, and approval sources.

humanMust: Sign in to the provider account, accept the relevant terms, and register the app under the correct owner.
Configure the exact integration callback and keep any client secret in secure server-side storage.
Consent with a test account and verify the intended API action, token handling, and any customer-admin restrictions.
Confirm production eligibility and complete any provider review required for the selected scopes and audience.
